<thought>Using the ESI‑MS data, the most intense ion is at m/z 183.0451. Assuming this is the [M+H]⁺ ion, the neutral monoisotopic mass is 183.0451 – 1.007276 ≈ 182.0378 Da. The isotopic pattern shows a strong M+2 peak (~33 % of the base), characteristic of a single chlorine atom (35Cl/37Cl). Subtracting the monoisotopic mass of 35Cl (34.968852 Da) leaves ≈147.069 Da to be composed of C, H, and O. The formula C₁₀H₁₁O (exact mass = 147.08099 Da) combined with one Cl gives a neutral mass of 182.04984 Da, which is within ~12 mDa (≈66 ppm) of the measured mass and best matches the observed isotopic pattern. Therefore the most plausible molecular formula is **C10H11OCl**.</thought>
<final_answer>C10H11OCl</final_answer>
